LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.headline: Seahawks’ Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Leonard Williams on injury report before Broncos game
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks have two key players to monitor ahead of their Week 6 Thursday Night Football matchup against the Denver Bronco s. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams remain limited with ankle injuries. Seattle released its second estimated injury report Tuesday (via Gregg Bell on X), with both players listed as limited participants for the second consecutive day. The Seahawks did not hold a physical practice because of their short week, meaning their participation designations reflect what the team estimates players would have done if practice had taken place. Seattle will release its final injury report Wednesday before Thursday night’s game in Denver. Williams is also working through an ankle injury that initially surfaced during Seattle’s Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. The veteran defensive tackle played against San Francisco, but his continued limited status is worth watching as the Seahawks prepare to face Denver’s offense. Seattle’s injury report features several other players, including linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf), who were both listed as non-participants. Running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and backup quarterback Drew Lock (right forearm) remained limited. On a positive note, guard Beau Stephens was upgraded to full participation, while running back George Holani and wide receiver Irvin Charles were also listed as full participants. Smith-Njigba suffered an ankle injury during the Seahawks’ 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday . Despite the issue, the star wide receiver finished the game with five receptions for 102 yards and a touchdown. He leads the NFL with 583 receiving yards through five games, making his availability a major storyline heading into the matchup against Denver. The Jags have back-to-back international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. The offensive line will be going up against defensive end Will Anderson Jr. , who has 27 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a league high, and one forced fumble and recovery this season. The Jags need to protect Trevor Lawrence, especially so he can continue to improve in his game-time decisions. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps. But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season. So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan. Predicted Stat Line: 30% snap share, 4 TAR, 3 REC, 43 YDS, 1 TD DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps . "Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do." So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks. Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. However, they are similarly big-bodied, outside receivers who can line up as a Z in several plays and situations, pairing pretty nicely next to the existing talent Houston has around the field at the position. Imagine Harrison Jr. simply slotting into those same snaps; likely with a bit more involvement in terms of being targeted or being a first read, but maybe not on the field for an excessive amount until he's able to get a few more weeks of practice and overall reps under his belt. A 30% snap share would likely be around the 15 to 20-snap mark. But in those limited looks, it feels likely that the Texans will involve him on a fair share of those plays––in this case, perhaps for four targets––to build up his confidence and rediscover some chemistry with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud . And in a best-case scenario for the Texans, maybe Harrison Jr. is able to haul in his second touchdown of the season so far. If Houston is within striking distance for a score, and there's an ideal situation for Harrison Jr. to fill into, why not start off the tenure with his new team on a good note? So in all, a 3-43-1 stat line feels like a modest projection for Harrison Jr. in game one. This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. away.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

away.headline: Caleb Williams Injury Update, Latest on QB's Status for Bears-Falcons, Severity of Hamstring Tear
away.blurb: "Before you start asking, (I) do not know if I'm playing yet," the Chicago Bears quarterback told reporters Thursday while revealing he still must undergo stress testing and pass medical protocols before he will be cleared to return. And while he seems to be ready to return, Williams said he wasn't happy with the reporting and reaction to his setback he called a "hamstring tear" that was "pretty serious." He was listed as a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day on Thursday, suggesting he is nearing a return. What's more, he also changed his Instagram profile picture to a photo of John Wick with a bio that read, "I'm inevitable." "He's doing a great job progressing and we'll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. "But he's itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we'll move forward from there." Caleb Williams is expected to start against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Williams previously said that he doesn't know if he would be on the field for Sunday's game. Williams suffered a hamstring injury during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. When he was carted off the field, Bears fans likely feared he would be lost for the season. Williams' status has been the biggest ongoing storyline surrounding the Bears. Johnson also said he believed the Bears "have three guys that can win games in this league." Chicago has done more than just tread water during Williams' absence, as Case Keenum led it to a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent directed a 23-12 win over the New York Jets. However, things took a turn last Sunday in a 31-7 blowout loss to the rival Green Bay Packers. Bagent started the game but played so poorly at 12-of-21 for 87 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions that Johnson put Keenum into the game to finish. It was a reminder the Bears likely need Williams healthy and under center quickly if they are going to have any realistic chance of repeating as NFC North champions. Now, it appears Williams will be back on the field this week.

For fantasy purposes, the line’s improved health makes Swift easier to trust. away.source: Chicago Bears On SI on MSN
away.blurb: But, as aforementioned, the Bears' 31-7 shellacking at the hands of the Packers should have served as a bucket of cold water over the heads of anyone who still entertained such ridiculous notions. The Bears' offense is severely limited without No. 18 under center, and no one is more eager than Williams himself to prove that on the field. Williams' return in Week 6 felt like a sure-thing ever since he landed on last Friday's injury report as 'Questionable', but now it's confirmed. The former No. 1 overall pick from the 2024 NFL draft is back and ready for action, and not a moment too soon. The Bears sit at 3-2 currently, leaving them in a three-way tie with the Packers and Detroit Lions for second place in the NFC North. They need to start stacking wins before their next divisional matchup in Week 12. Caleb Williams Reposts Electric Hype Video Hinting at Return For Bears vs. Falcons This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/bears/onsi as Bears' Caleb Williams Makes Official Return from Injury in Week 6 vs Falcons . For the first time since Week 2, the Chicago Bears will finally have their starting quarterback under center. According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo , Caleb Williams has passed all the tests for his injured hamstring and is good to go for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Though Bears fans widely expected Williams to be back after a full week of practice, and especially after he reposted an electric hype video on social media, it has to feel good to get this official confirmation. The Bears went 2-1 in Williams' absence, a good record for any team to hit without their starting quarterback, but a disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers reminded everyone just how badly Williams is missed. Caleb Williams has plenty to prove after his time on the sidelines While he's always played with something of a chip on his shoulder, one has to believe that Williams is coming into tomorrow's game with a vengeance. His hamstring injury created memes and jokes across all social media, most of which were unfair and wildly ignorant. Critics and podcasters created a bizarre narrative that Williams, who had started and finished 35 consecutive regular season games before his injury, was soft and not built for the NFL. While that is quite literally adding insult to injury, it didn't stop there. Backup quarterbacks Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent both led the Bears to one win apiece in Williams' absence, which fueled wild theories about whether the Bears even needed Williams. It was as if the central role he played in the Bears' 59-point Week 1 thriller against the Carolina Panthers had never happened. Between Williams wanting to remind the NFL world of who he is and sheer necessity, I would hate to be the Falcons' defense tomorrow. home.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

home.headline: Caleb Williams Injury Update, Latest on QB's Status for Bears-Falcons, Severity of Hamstring Tear
home.blurb: "Before you start asking, (I) do not know if I'm playing yet," the Chicago Bears quarterback told reporters Thursday while revealing he still must undergo stress testing and pass medical protocols before he will be cleared to return. And while he seems to be ready to return, Williams said he wasn't happy with the reporting and reaction to his setback he called a "hamstring tear" that was "pretty serious." He was listed as a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day on Thursday, suggesting he is nearing a return. What's more, he also changed his Instagram profile picture to a photo of John Wick with a bio that read, "I'm inevitable." "He's doing a great job progressing and we'll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. "But he's itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we'll move forward from there." Caleb Williams is expected to start against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Williams previously said that he doesn't know if he would be on the field for Sunday's game. Williams suffered a hamstring injury during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. When he was carted off the field, Bears fans likely feared he would be lost for the season. Williams' status has been the biggest ongoing storyline surrounding the Bears. Johnson also said he believed the Bears "have three guys that can win games in this league." Chicago has done more than just tread water during Williams' absence, as Case Keenum led it to a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent directed a 23-12 win over the New York Jets. However, things took a turn last Sunday in a 31-7 blowout loss to the rival Green Bay Packers. Bagent started the game but played so poorly at 12-of-21 for 87 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions that Johnson put Keenum into the game to finish. It was a reminder the Bears likely need Williams healthy and under center quickly if they are going to have any realistic chance of repeating as NFC North champions. Now, it appears Williams will be back on the field this week.

home.headline: Bears' Caleb Williams Makes Official Return from Injury in Week 6 vs Falcons
home.source: Chicago Bears On SI on MSN
home.blurb: But, as aforementioned, the Bears' 31-7 shellacking at the hands of the Packers should have served as a bucket of cold water over the heads of anyone who still entertained such ridiculous notions. The Bears' offense is severely limited without No. 18 under center, and no one is more eager than Williams himself to prove that on the field. Williams' return in Week 6 felt like a sure-thing ever since he landed on last Friday's injury report as 'Questionable', but now it's confirmed. The former No. 1 overall pick from the 2024 NFL draft is back and ready for action, and not a moment too soon. The Bears sit at 3-2 currently, leaving them in a three-way tie with the Packers and Detroit Lions for second place in the NFC North. They need to start stacking wins before their next divisional matchup in Week 12. Caleb Williams Reposts Electric Hype Video Hinting at Return For Bears vs. Falcons This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/bears/onsi as Bears' Caleb Williams Makes Official Return from Injury in Week 6 vs Falcons . For the first time since Week 2, the Chicago Bears will finally have their starting quarterback under center. According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo , Caleb Williams has passed all the tests for his injured hamstring and is good to go for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Though Bears fans widely expected Williams to be back after a full week of practice, and especially after he reposted an electric hype video on social media, it has to feel good to get this official confirmation. The Bears went 2-1 in Williams' absence, a good record for any team to hit without their starting quarterback, but a disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers reminded everyone just how badly Williams is missed. Caleb Williams has plenty to prove after his time on the sidelines While he's always played with something of a chip on his shoulder, one has to believe that Williams is coming into tomorrow's game with a vengeance. His hamstring injury created memes and jokes across all social media, most of which were unfair and wildly ignorant. Critics and podcasters created a bizarre narrative that Williams, who had started and finished 35 consecutive regular season games before his injury, was soft and not built for the NFL. While that is quite literally adding insult to injury, it didn't stop there. Backup quarterbacks Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent both led the Bears to one win apiece in Williams' absence, which fueled wild theories about whether the Bears even needed Williams. It was as if the central role he played in the Bears' 59-point Week 1 thriller against the Carolina Panthers had never happened. Between Williams wanting to remind the NFL world of who he is and sheer necessity, I would hate to be the Falcons' defense tomorrow. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the fifth straight week in a row now, we can say that the Tennessee Titans fell short of expectations. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. In an AFC South-bound duel tomorrow, I unfortunately anticipate the losing streak to continue. All we can hope for is a surprise from Saleh and a squad that, up to now, haven't done near enough to spark midseason hope. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. away.headline: Colts Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon Against Titans
away.blurb: Several key players appear to be trending in the right direction, but Indianapolis has already ruled out two contributors, and rookie tight end Tyler Warren remains questionable. Through five games, he has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns, trailing only Josh Downs in receiving yards for Indianapolis. Losing him would be a massive blow to a passing attack that is already running out of healthy weapons. Alec Pierce remains on injured reserve, Darius Slayton was released Friday without ever appearing in a game for Indianapolis, and Dulin has now been ruled out for a second straight week. Will Mallory practiced fully all week as he works his way back from a thumb injury, although he is also listed as questionable while Indianapolis decides whether to activate him from injured reserve. Jonathan Taylor logged his second consecutive full practice, while Jalen Travis progressed from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday and full participation Friday. Grover Stewart returned to full participation after a rest day Thursday, while Charvarius Ward has now practiced fully on back-to-back days. DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday, but his absence was rest-related. Carlies being out for a second straight week still hurts a linebacker room that has struggled early this season, but Warren's status carries the biggest offensive implications. With an already depleted receiving corps, having Warren available could be the difference between an offense that finds its rhythm and another frustrating afternoon for Daniel Jones. Friday brought a mixed bag of injury news for the Indianapolis Colts ahead of Sunday's AFC South matchup with the Tennessee Titans. Of all the developments on Friday's report, Warren's status is easily the one that concerns me most. Tyler Warren Remains the Biggest Question Mark Warren was arguably the only bright spot for this offense in last week's 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh, catching seven passes for 83 yards and adding a one-yard rushing touchdown. That leaves Keenan Allen, Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks as the primary wide receiver options, with Warren's status potentially making things even thinner. Warren wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday, making his late-week appearance with a groin injury even more concerning. The good news is Allen and Downs have logged two straight full practices after lighter workloads Wednesday. Daniel Jones was also a full participant all three days despite remaining on the report with an ankle designation. Most of the Report Trended in the Right Direction Outside of Warren, Carlies and Dulin, Friday was fairly encouraging. Tennessee owns PFF's 26th-ranked coverage unit through five weeks, which should give Indianapolis an opportunity to attack through the air. But without Pierce, Dulin and potentially Warren, I am not sure the Colts have enough firepower to fully take advantage. That could put even more pressure on Downs and Taylor. away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . home.headline: Colts Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon Against Titans
home.blurb: Several key players appear to be trending in the right direction, but Indianapolis has already ruled out two contributors, and rookie tight end Tyler Warren remains questionable. Through five games, he has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns, trailing only Josh Downs in receiving yards for Indianapolis. Losing him would be a massive blow to a passing attack that is already running out of healthy weapons. Alec Pierce remains on injured reserve, Darius Slayton was released Friday without ever appearing in a game for Indianapolis, and Dulin has now been ruled out for a second straight week. Will Mallory practiced fully all week as he works his way back from a thumb injury, although he is also listed as questionable while Indianapolis decides whether to activate him from injured reserve. Jonathan Taylor logged his second consecutive full practice, while Jalen Travis progressed from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday and full participation Friday. Grover Stewart returned to full participation after a rest day Thursday, while Charvarius Ward has now practiced fully on back-to-back days. DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday, but his absence was rest-related. Carlies being out for a second straight week still hurts a linebacker room that has struggled early this season, but Warren's status carries the biggest offensive implications. With an already depleted receiving corps, having Warren available could be the difference between an offense that finds its rhythm and another frustrating afternoon for Daniel Jones. Friday brought a mixed bag of injury news for the Indianapolis Colts ahead of Sunday's AFC South matchup with the Tennessee Titans. Of all the developments on Friday's report, Warren's status is easily the one that concerns me most. Tyler Warren Remains the Biggest Question Mark Warren was arguably the only bright spot for this offense in last week's 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh, catching seven passes for 83 yards and adding a one-yard rushing touchdown. That leaves Keenan Allen, Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks as the primary wide receiver options, with Warren's status potentially making things even thinner. Warren wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday, making his late-week appearance with a groin injury even more concerning. The good news is Allen and Downs have logged two straight full practices after lighter workloads Wednesday. Daniel Jones was also a full participant all three days despite remaining on the report with an ankle designation. Most of the Report Trended in the Right Direction Outside of Warren, Carlies and Dulin, Friday was fairly encouraging. Tennessee owns PFF's 26th-ranked coverage unit through five weeks, which should give Indianapolis an opportunity to attack through the air. But without Pierce, Dulin and potentially Warren, I am not sure the Colts have enough firepower to fully take advantage. That could put even more pressure on Downs and Taylor. home.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
home.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . home.headline: Colts activate TE Will Mallory from IR
home.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts activated Will Mallory from injured reserve on Saturday, one day after they listed fellow tight end Tyler Warren as questionable with a groin injury that he sustained in practice. Mallory's questionable status was lifted from the injury report by the Colts (2-3) ahead of Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans (0-5) in Indianapolis. Mallory, 27, has 23 catches for 252 yards in 24 career games (two starts) with the Colts. He was selected by Indianapolis in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Miami. He had been on injured reserve since Aug. 30 with a thumb injury. A Pro Bowl selection in his rookie season in 2025, Warren has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns in five games (all starts) this season. Warren, 24, also has a touchdown run. The Patriots upset the Bills in Buffalo two weeks ago then put up 45 points in a blowout win against the Raiders last week. The Jets are also feeling good after a 17-12 win against the Browns. They had lost their previous three contests after opening the season with a victory in Tennessee. New England has won three straight meetings against the Jets, including 42-10 and 27-14 last year. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 6 matchup with a final score prediction. Jets vs. Patriots Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jets +7.5 (-115) Patriots -7.5 (-105) Patriots: -325 43.5 (Over -112/Under -108) Line Movement: The spread hasn’t moved since the odds opened for this matchup, but the total has gone down a point from 44.5 to 43.5. Jets vs. Patriots Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: The Jets may not be as bad as I thought they'd be this season. They aren't good, but they're ranked around the middle of the pack in the NFL across many metrics, including 20th in EPA per play, 11th in opponent EPA per play, and 14th in net yards per play (+0.2). Geno Smith has also been interesting this season. He hasn't been throwing the ball all over the field and racking up yards, but he's been accurate, ranking 10th in completion percentage over expected, and he has yet to throw an interception. Efficient play from your quarterback goes a long way in covering spreads as an underdog. The Patriots are coming off an impressive win against the Raiders last week, but let's not pretend that all of their early-season problems have been solved. I'm not sure I'm ready to back them to cover a 7.5-point spread against a division rival this week. Pick: Jets +7.5 (-115) via FanDuel I think I disagree with MacMillan on this one. The Patriots have put up two dominating wins in their first two home games. They beat the Steelers 20-3 as -4.5 favorites in Week 2 and covered as just -3.5 favorites in the blowout last week. The Jets may be able to keep this from being a complete blowout, but I think the Patriots can pull away at home. New York has failed to cover in both of its road losses. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. The New England Patriots (-7.5) will look to make it three straight wins when they host the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on Sunday afternoon. New York and New England both boast defenses that can keep opposing offenses in check, so I'm taking the Under in my Jets vs. Patriots prediction . Keep reading to see all my free NFL picks for Sunday, Oct. 18. TOP Pick Jets vs Patriots prediction: Under 43.5 The New York Jets may be better than their 2-3 record suggests, but only because of their defense. The Jets offense averages 5.1 yards per play, 22nd in the NFL, and ranks 28th in scoring at 18.6 ppg. The New England Patriots have turned the ball over on offense over the last two weeks, but they aren't as good as the 37.0 ppg they've averaged in that span, and they aren't as bad as the 12.0 ppg they put up before that. The New York defense is top three in the NFL in yards allowed per play (4.9) and yards allowed per passing attempt (5.5), which should tamp down on Drake Maye's outstanding numbers over the past two weeks. I'm backing the Under to 42.5 points. Jets vs Patriots combo I'm not expecting many points in this game, and on its face, that makes me suspicious of a spread of more than a touchdown. Even in the Jets' three losses this year, they've only lost by more than one score once in a 23-12 defeat to the Chicago Bears . I'm taking New York to cover. One area where the Patriots might consistently succeed is the running game, where the Jets allow 4.2 yards per rush. Rhamondre Stevenson is coming off a 64-yard performance against the Las Vegas Raiders last week, and I see him hitting the 60+ yard target on the ground again on Sunday. Rhamondre Stevenson Over 62.5 rushing yards Jets vs Patriots touchdown scorer: Hunter Henry Hunter Henry has had his two most productive games of the year over the past two weeks. He caught 8 passes for 106 yards and scored a touchdown last Sunday against the Raiders. The Jets haven't allowed a tight end touchdown yet this year, but have given up 22 catches for 183 yards to the group . New England won't spring many explosive plays against New York's secondary, and Henry will get plenty of red-zone targets. I like Henry to score a touchdown at 36% or lower. Could this be the time when they finally achieve that, or will they be hanging on to relevance by a thread once again after Sunday? Let's break down the Patriots' roster going position by position: Drake Maye is coming off a season where he was a legitimate MVP candidate. However, after three weeks, he wasn't playing like that. The Patriots were 1-2 as Maye had thrown six interceptions and just one touchdown pass. However, he's rediscovered himself over the past two games, leading New England to a come-from-behind win against the Bills and a blowout of the Raiders. His 374 yard output against the Raiders represented the second-highest total of his career, as he completed multiple deep balls. Over the two wins, he had seven touchdowns and just one interception. The Patriots' number two is Tommy DeVito, who won three straight games as an undrafted rookie with the Giants but hasn't had much success since then. Seventh round rookie Behren Morton is the number three. Offensive Line New England has a question mark on their offensive line this week after left tackle Will Campbell was injured and knocked out of the previous game. Campbell has been practicing on a limited basis all week but his game status is uncertain and he's listed as questionable. In last week's game, first round pick Caleb Lomu stepped in for Campbell and did well. In college, Lomu faced David Bailey and handled him well, although this was while Bailey was still at Stanford, so he hadn't fully broken out yet. New England has multiple ex-Jets on their offensive line with Morgan Moses at right tackle and Alijah Vera-Tucker at left guard. They also have Greg Van Roten, but he's on injured reserve. The 35-year old Moses is doing a solid job, although he does have five penalties in five games. So far, the injury-prone Vera-Tucker has been completely healthy with the Patriots. The other starters are last year's third round pick Jared Wilson at center and veteran Mike Onwenu at right guard. However, Onwenu is also on injured reserve, so Ben Brown is currently starting there. Matt Pryor, Walter Rouse and sixth round rookie Dametrious Crownover are available as cover. Rouse already had to fill in for 41 snaps in week three. In the event of an injury to Wilson, Brown would probably slide across to center. Running Backs Similar to Campbell, running back TreVeyon Henderson has practiced on a limited basis this week but his status is uncertain after he picked up a high ankle sprain in last week's game. He has said he feels pretty good but has been listed as questionable with New England also perhaps thinking ahead to their matchup with the Bears next Thursday. Henderson had 900 yards and nine touchdowns last year, but Rhamondre Stevenson is a more than adequate replacement, who has been a thousand-yard back in the past. He leads the team in rushing yards so far this year. The number three is Corey Kiner, who saw some playing time last week but fumbled once. Pass catchers The Patriots activated AJ Brown for practice this week, after he had been injured in the opener, so he may return to give their offense a further boost on Sunday, although his official game status is questionable. In Brown's absence, Mack Hollins had been leading the team in receptions, but he is also now on injured reserve. Offseason signing Romeo Doubs leads the team with 219 receiving yards and Pop Douglas is coming off a game last week where he caught two touchdown passes. Slot receiver Efton Chism is now a regular part of the rotation and responded with the winning touchdown against the Bills on a spectacular one-handed catch. Kyle Williams also gets regular playing time and has been established as a big play threat. At tight end, Hunter Henry is off to a modest start, having caught 60 passes with seven touchdowns last year. Third round rookie Eli Raridon is the number two, and has eight catches with a touchdown, while Tanner Arkin and Cameron Latu are also on the roster with Julian Hill on injured reserve. Defensive Line The starters on the defensive line are former first round pick Christian Barmore, nose tackle Cory Durden and last year's big money signing Milton Williams, who had 3.5 sacks. DaQuan Jones gives them an experienced backup at the nose tackle position with Joshua Farmer and ex-Jet Leonard Taylor III also on the team. All six of these players were active in the Raiders game, although Taylor has played the least on defense. New England are without their top two pass rushers from last season, as K'Lavon Chaisson left during the offseason and Harold Landry is on the PUP list. These two combined for 16 sacks last season. In their place, the starters on the edge are Elijah Ponder and Dre'Mont Jones, with Ponder having really stepped up so far as he has 4.5 sacks and leads the team in quarterback hits and tackles for loss. Second round rookie Gabe Jacas is likely to see his role continue to expand though, as he's flashed playmaking abilities as a rotational player with 1.5 sacks, an interception, three tackles for loss and five quarterback hits. The inside linebackers are led by Robert Spillane, who had 97 tackles last season and is leading the team again in that category. Alongside him, Christian Elliss also plays a full time role. Elliss is another Patriots player who is listed as questionable, although he practiced full on Friday. The reserves on the inside are Erick Hunter, Darius Muasau and sixth round rookie Namdi Obiazor, although they don't play much. All three got some valuable reps in garbage time last week though. Defensive Backs New England has some real talent at cornerback with their three starters all having posted double digits for passes defensed last year. Former first round pick Christian Gonzalez was a pro bowler and the slot cornerback Marcus Jones intercepted three passes last year to prove he's not just a punt returner. Carlton Davis was a big money signing who slotted well into the rotation. Davis has been ruled out due to injury and Gonzalez also had some injury issues, but he appears to be good to go. The main backup is Charles Woods, so he may need to step in for Davis. Fifth round rookie Karon Prunty, Channing Canada and Kindle Vildor are the other backups, but Prunty has been ruled out and Canada is listed as questionable. At safety New England brought in Kevin Byard to replace Jaylinn Hawkins, who had led them with four interceptions in 2025. Craig Woodson returns as the other starter with Dell Pettus on injured reserve. Woodson is also listed as questionable but was not limited in practice on Friday, so should be fine to play. Jaylen Reed has also started one game and seen action in three-safety sets, while Mike Brown is available in reserve and Brenden Schooler is mostly just a special teamer. Special Teams Kicker Andy Borregales missed seven kicks last season and has already missed two this year. He had the game winner against the Bills last season and also had the game-winner against Denver in the AFC title game, albeit in the third quarter. Punter Brian Baringer is on injured reserve so veteran Mitch Wishnowsky currently has this role. He has a net average of below 40 yards but has only allowed 64 return yards. In the return game, Jones is a two-time all pro as a punt returner and once had the game winning score against the Jets (albeit due to an obvious missed holding penalty). He had two more touchdowns last year. Douglas is listed as his backup, while Williams handles kickoffs with Chism as his number two. The pro bowler Schooler has only played one game so far this year, but the Patriots have plenty of other productive players in kick coverage, including Elliss, Ponder, Obiazor, Hunter and Muasau. The backup cornerbacks share the gunner roles along with Schooler.

away.blurb: The Jets will be without two important offensive playmakers against New England, but the return of a promising young rookie provides some much-needed optimism. Let's start with the bad. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that two key weapons on the offense, in both running back Breece Hall, who has a quad injury, and wide receiver AD Mitchell, who has a finger injury, have been ruled out for Sunday's game against New England. That's not how it played out. Hall sat out against Chicago, missed last week's win over the Cleveland Browns , and now he's going to miss a third straight game. Look, at this point, the Jets could have put him on IR and freed up a roster spot. They haven't done that, and for whatever reason, the team keeps holding the door open for a return that hasn't come. That's been frustrating to watch. I'm high on both of these guys. Cooper gives the Jets a receiver who can take attention away from Wilson on the outside, and Sadiq is a matchup problem for linebackers and safeties. With Hall and Mitchell out, the Jets need their young talent to step up, and this is the perfect spot for both rookies to show what they can do. Losing Mitchell on top of Hall stings, too. The game gives the Saints an opportunity to take on what may end up a division winner in the NFC East. The game presents a shot at a morale-boosting win and one that the Saints could build on to get out of their current rut. The Giants, however, do not intend to go down that easily. ESPN NFL insider Katherine Terrell shared the latest on the Saints heading into the matchup. Here's some of what Terrell wrote alongside other ESPN experts. There's frustration to go around after the Saints' third straight loss, and owner Gayle Benson made a rare public statement commenting on how the team's current record is not acceptable. QB Tyler Shough says he understands and shares her frustration. "She wasn't saying anything that wasn't already known, and she did a really good job of highlighting the expectations, and we have those same expectations for ourselves," he said. -- Fellow ESPN NFL insider Jordan Raanan gave intel on the Giants. Here's some of what Raanan had to say. "The Giants are playing at home and became underdogs as the week progressed. That didn't seem to sit well with the team. 'We love playing at MetLife Stadium and being underdogs,' defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said. 'Everybody counts us out.' The Giants are admittedly playing with a chip on their shoulders after RB Cam Skattebo said it was dumb for them to be underdogs in their previous home game against the Cardinals." In a noteworthy prediction, Seth Walder had the Saints winning the game 20-14. If the Saints can hold an opponent to 14 points, it would be a huge win for the defensive unit. New Orleans held the Minnesota Vikings to 23 points in a 23-13 loss, and even that felt like an improvement. We'd like to see more improvement in Week 6. Per ESPN, the Saints have a 53.9% chance to pull off the win with just a one-point advantage in simulations. Needless to say, the prediction certainly indicates two evenly matched teams. We may not have reached true must-win territory, but we're getting close. Look for the Saints to bring their best effort in search of their second win of the season.
