picks.headline: Chris Olave's 537 Yards Run Into Jevon Holland's NFL-Leading 3 Picks in Saints-Giants Showdown
picks.blurb: Chris Olave's 537 Yards Run Into Jevon Holland's NFL-Leading 3 Picks in Saints-Giants Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up College football live updates A.J. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chris Olave has been the one part of the Saints' offense nobody in the French Quarter is complaining about. The problem Sunday is that the New York Giants have a safety who has spent the season taking the ball away, and Jevon Holland will be waiting on every deep throw Tyler Shough sends Olave's way at MetLife Stadium. We noted this week that Olave is playing at an elite level , and it hasn't been close. Olave has 537 receiving yards, second in the NFL, and he's run 205 routes, more than any receiver in the league, according to PFF . His 89.4 overall grade ranks eighth among 86 qualifying wideouts, and his average depth of target sits at 13.4 yards. That's a lot of downfield work for a receiver who played through a foot scare against Minnesota. Holland is the league leader in interceptions with three, and he picked one off in each of the first three weeks, earning NFC Defensive Player of the Month honors for September. He's allowed just three receptions and a 40.8 passer rating in coverage, with an 86.3 overall grade that ranks fourth among 96 safeties, per PFF . He also has two forced fumbles. Where the Olave-Holland duel will be decided Sep 20, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) looks on from the sideline in the second quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn ImagesJamie Sabau-Imagn Images Olave won't see Holland on every snap, since Holland plays deep and Olave works outside. The collision comes on the throws that define Olave's season: the deep crossers and go routes where Shough has to trust his receiver to win late. Giants coach John Harbaugh already knows it. "Those two guys, they're a connection right now," he said of Shough and Olave in the AP preview . That connection is also where Shough's mistakes have shown up. Shough has five interceptions on 205 attempts and called one of his picks against Minnesota "a stupid decision," as we wrote earlier this week . Holland made his name in Week 3 by sealing a win over Tennessee with an interception on the penultimate play . "This defense is definitely very sound," Holland said after earning the monthly award . If the Giants' blitzers force Shough to hurry, Holland gets more chances to read the quarterback's eyes and jump a route meant for Olave. Olave's status is worth watching, too. He missed practice early in the week with an illness and is listed as questionable . If he plays and wins two or three of those deep shots without feeding Holland a fourth pick, the Saints have a real path to snapping a three-game losing streak in New Jersey. away.blurb: That original timeline now approaches its two-month mark, but Tyson still isn't ready to return to practice. The rookie began the regular season on injured reserve, meaning he had to miss at least the first four games before becoming eligible to return. That minimum absence has passed, but his recovery has yet to reach the point where the Saints are comfortable allowing him to practice. Moore's announcement does not establish a new timetable for Tyson's return or indicate that he suffered another setback. With Tyson ruled out of practice this week, a debut against New York is effectively off the table. Whether he can return in time for the Steelers game will depend on his progress over the following week. That creates a potentially useful recovery window if Tyson cannot return before the team's trip to Paris, although the Saints have not identified a specific game as his target. Saints head coach Kellen Moore announced Monday, October 12, that rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson will not practice this week as he continues recovering from a hamstring injury. The disappointing update comes as New Orleans prepares to face the New York Giants on October 18, following a 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings that dropped the Saints to 1-4. Tyson, the No. 8 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft, has yet to make his regular-season debut. And with no practice work scheduled this week, his availability remains a significant concern for a Saints offense still searching for consistency. Saints' Jordyn Tyson Still Recovering From Hamstring Injury Tyson's injury has already kept him sidelined considerably longer than New Orleans originally hoped when it selected him in April. The former Arizona State standout suffered a hamstring injury during training camp in August, with N FL Network insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reporting on August 17 that he was expected to miss approximately two months. New Orleans has been cautious with Tyson throughout the process. Moore previously acknowledged uncertainty surrounding the receiver's practice timeline, and Monday's announcement confirms that the waiting continues. home.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Olave Questionable as Giants Face Offensive Line Concerns Skip to main content SI.COM The Saints' top receiving target, Chris Olave , who missed the last two practices with an illness, was a limited participant Friday. If Olave can play Sunday, starting quarterback Tyler Shough can breathe a sigh of relief. On defense, linebacker Kaden Elliss and edge rusher Anfernee Jennings are out again for Sunday. As for the Giants, edge rusher Abdul Carter and starting offensive tackles Jermaine Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas have been listed as questionable. Olave has recorded 39 catches for 537 yards with a touchdown. Olave is second in the league in receiving yards and is tied for third in receptions. Elliss, who is arguably the Saints’ best player at his position, has been greatly missed as the Saints have allowed 179 yards per game on the ground since his injury during their 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3. Concerns about Season Reach the Top After Saints owner Gayle Benson said the Saints’ 1-4 start was “unacceptable” earlier in the week, head coach Kellen Moore said after practice he speaks with her regularly and communicated with her throughout the week. The availability of both Eluemunor and Thomas could have major implications for Sunday's matchup, particularly against a solid edge rusher rotation of New Orleans’ Carl Granderson , Chase Young and Cameron Jordan . LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. away.headline: Eagles place QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on IR ahead of game vs. Panthers
away.blurb: The Eagles believe the blood clot is treatable, but Hurts’ medical team will determine when the 28-year-old can return to play, according to the reports. The Eagles’ decision to put Hurts on IR came after consultations with several doctors and experts, ESPN and the NFL Network reported. Hurts must miss at least four games, beginning Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, followed by matchups with the Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants. Philadelphia (2-3), which has lost three straight, then has a Week 10 bye, when the Eagles will reevaluate Hurts’ health and the team’s outlook, per ESPN and NFL Network. In five games this season, Hurts has passed for 933 yards and eight touchdowns, with three interceptions. Doctors discovered the blood clot during an Oct. 10 ultrasound after Hurts sustained a calf injury against the Los Angeles Rams on Oct. 4. They cleared him to play against Jacksonville the following day, when he completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown without an interception in a 19-17 loss. However, a follow-up ultrasound Wednesday showed the clot moving, prompting further evaluation. Eagles backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers, and rookie Cole Payton was promoted to backup. Philadelphia also signed quarterback Joe Milton off Dallas’ practice squad. away.headline: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return
away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. home.headline: Jalen Hurts injury situation takes another scary turn that leaves the Philadelphia Eagles with plenty of questions
home.blurb: The concern for Hurts' health became evident rather quickly once the team issued a statement on his status. Blood clots are no joke and can create significant health risks - and it seems that Hurts' circumstances go beyond that of a superficial issue that needed a quick fix. So now, it's the Tanner McKee show for the Eagles behind center - the latest in a series of blows to the Eagles' offense this season. You almost couldn't have scripted a more chaotic script at the beginning of the season if you tried. The star running back injures his hamstring. The All-Pro right tackle abruptly retires. A staple of the interior is traded away. And now, blood clots land the starting quarterback on injured reserve. Presumably for an indefinite period of time. Life comes at you fast. And for Hurts in particular, there should be no rush on a return timeline. All this does for Philadelphia is affirm what we already knew. This season is off the rails. Hurts is out for "the foreseeable future". He, like the Eagles, must now turn their attention to a long-term view. Best wishes in his recovery - and who knows what this team will look like when he's ready to return. home.headline: Robert Griffin III rips former NFL player over Jalen Hurts’ Eagles injury take
home.blurb: Earlier this week, stunning news arrived that Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot discovered before the team’s London game earlier this month. He’s been receiving treatment for the superficial blood clot, also known as superficial thrombophlebitis , and practiced fully this past Wednesday ahead of the Panthers game. However, the team revealed that new ultrasound findings led to him being ruled out for Sunday’s game. “On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority,” the team’s statement said on Thursday. “Michael Robinson is accusing Jalen Hurts of saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ And that Jalen Hurts is ‘pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.’ when Jalen Hurts has a BLOOD CLOT THAT SHOWED MOVEMENT AND COULD BE LIFE THREATENING,” Griffin III wrote. Griffin III hasn’t played since the Baltimore Ravens released him in early 2021 and has since moved into podcasting and appearances on various Fox Sports programs to share his insights. His calling out of Robinson on X made clear that he believes Hurts’ health takes priority over criticism of the Eagles quarterback and the team’s struggles. ESPN’s Tim McManus reported that Hurts was a full participant in Eagles practice last Friday ahead of the Sunday matchup in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He then “played without limitation” in that game, which the Eagles lost, 19-17. Amid the concerning health issue Hurts is experiencing, former Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers fullback Michael Robinson shared a controversial take on NFL Network’s “NFL Gameday.” He suggested, while playing “devil’s advocate,” that with the Eagles potentially linking their struggles to Hurts, he could be using the injury to distance himself from that blame. Read more: Ex-NFL Star Draws Major Backlash for Controversial Jalen Hurts Take Robert Griffin III, a former Heisman Trophy winner and NFL quarterback, fired off his response to Robinson’s take calling it “RIDICULOUS.” “The negative narratives around Jalen Hurts have to stop,” he wrote in an X message sharing the clip of Robinson. “That’s OUTRAGEOUS @RealMikeRob WHAT ARE WE DOING MAN? I would never expect this from a former player. I wouldn’t expect this from ANYBODY,” he wrote, ending with, “Jalen Hurts can’t even have a serious medical condition in peace.” Griffin III was the Washington Commanders’ No. 2 pick in the 2012 NFL Draft and became the league’s Offensive Rookie of the Year. Many believed he could become the next superstar quarterback, but unfortunately, a severe knee injury during the Commanders’ playoff run and subsequent injuries derailed his career. home.blurb: "I know what I can do. I genuinely know what I can do. I know the impact I can have on this game," Greenard said on Friday. "I still feel like I'm one of the best at my position. I like myself against anybody. It's just a matter of me getting out there and showing it." The timing of Greenard's return is important as Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) is out and A.J. Epenesa (back) is doubtful. "Our injury report is longer than a novel. It's crazy, man. It's insane," Greenard said. "At the same time, we play a very physically demanding sport. When you're at this point, like we are with the Eagles, you're going to get the best from everybody. You got to make sure you bring it day in and day out. "Nobody is going to come save us, so we have to come get ourselves out of this hole. And we like that. We are not a losing team. We're maybe doing some loser things at times, but we're not a losing team and everybody knows that, so I'm excited to see what we do on Sunday." Wide receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle) and safety Marcus Epps (groin) are also set to return from injury. Center Drew Kendall was limited in practice on both Thursday and Friday. He's questionable for Sunday. The Eagles opened the practice window this week for cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee), tight end Grant Calcaterra (back), guard Landon Dickerson (knee), and tight end Eli Stowers (knee). It remains to be seen whether the Panthers will activate tackle Taylor Moton (lungs, blood clot) or defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton (neck) from Injured Reserve. Both players were full participants in practice all week, but are officially questionable for Sunday. Moton's potential return would mitigate the likely loss of rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling, who is doubtful with a knee injury. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? away.blurb: Patterson played for the Steelers in 2024, his final stop in the NFL. The four-time Pro Bowler and seven-time All-Pro selection played 12 years and finished his career with the most kickoffs returned for touchdowns with nine, plus the longest kick return for a touchdown of 109 yards. As a kick returner, Patterson struggled. The two-time kick return yards leader only had 11 returns in 2024, totaling 240 yards. He was among the NFL's worst, averaging just 21.8 yards per return. Last season, Pittsburgh replaced Patterson with running back Jaylen Warren and Kenny Gainwell. Gainwell led the team with 26 returns for 633 yards, averaging 24.3 yards per return. He was eventually named the Team MVP after the season. Steelers On SI will continue to release updates as more information on Patterson's arrest becomes available. away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he's caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who's handled a heavy workload in Dowdle's absence. picks.headline: Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams
picks.blurb: Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up College football live updates A.J. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Roberts, Editor Toussaint Fancher Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a disappointing end to Week 5 , the Los Angeles Rams look to get back in the win column against the Arizona Cardinals. "I love Mike [LaFleur], and it's about the Rams versus the Cardinals, and we're going to try to get after him as good as we can this week," Rams head coach Sean McVay said about facing the Cardinals. The Rams will face the Cardinals in the first matchup against former Los Angeles offensive coordinator, Mike LaFleur. LaFleur spent the past two seasons as the Rams' offensive coordinator, and now they will face off for the first time since LaFleur became Arizona's head coach. Last week, the Los Angeles Rams had a great offensive game. The offense was electric as the game became a barnburner. Buffalo and their quarterback Josh Allen were unstoppable on the ground and got the best of the Los Angeles defense. This week, the Rams face the Arizona Cardinals, who are currently 1-4 and on a three-game losing streak. While the Rams must approach every game with the same level of preparation, the Cardinals are an easier opponent than the Bills. Although the Cardinals are an easier matchup, they still have plenty of playmakers. Michael Wilson, Jeremiyah Love and Trey McBride are a few of their top tier players who can change the game at a moment's notice. The Cardinals quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, is an experienced veteran who can play his best at any moment. Last season, the journeyman threw for over 3,300 yards with 23 touchdowns – both career highs. The Cardinals are a wildcard on any given game, but the Rams should be able to handle Arizona easily. Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams place kicker Harrison Mevis (92) kicks a point after try during the fourth quarter against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images After the Week 5 loss to the Bills, the Rams made big changes, specifically to the special teams unit. Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis after his poor performance. Mevis missed a 50-yard field attempt and also had a game leading 48-yard field goal blocked in overtime. Rams also released returner and wide receiver Xavier Smith – marred by his costly turnover in the NFC championship game last season. The Rams signed Blake Grupe off the New York Jets' practice squad as a replacement. Last season, he played for the Indianapolis Colts and the New Orleans Saints, going 29 for 37 with a long of 60 yards. The Rams' special teams has been the league's worst under McVay since he became head coach. McVay stood behind his special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone after the loss. "I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone," said McVay on Tuesday. "There are no changes that are going to be made there. We're going to keep working. This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of." Following Monday Night's game, the NFL suspended Rams starting left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb. Jackson appealed and his suspension was reduced to one game. Jackson will miss this week's matchup against the Cardinals before returning next week against the Las Vegas Raiders. While no players have been listed out for the game, several were on the injury report or missed practice this week. Tight end Davis Allen was listed as Did Not Participate (DNP) due to a foot injury, and Omar Speights, Nate Landman, Colby Parkinson and Kam Curl were all limited participants. The Last Word Even though the Rams are 2-3, they are still in a good place. The next five games are all winnable, they must remain focused on their opponent each week. The Rams have started 2-3 or worse in four of their six seasons with quarterback Matthew Stafford. In 2023, the Rams started 2-3 and the following year saw a 1-4 start. Despite the slow starts, the Rams made the playoffs in both seasons. The Rams are also waiting on the return of Myles Garrett to pair his extraordinary talents with Aaron Donald. The Rams still have a tough task ahead and need to focus on coming away with a victory on Sunday. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals injury report: Jeremiyah Love sits Wednesday
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. Head coach Mike LaFleur said on Monday he won't clear it this week before they play the LA Rams on Sunday. With Andrew Wingard still dealing with a knee injury, that would leave only Budda Baker and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson healthy and available. However, help could be on the way, as Kitan Crawford was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday and had his 21-day practice window opened. That move allows him to start practice despite still being on injured reserve, and he can be reinstated to the active roster at anytime during that window. If he has not been reinstated at the conclusion of the 21 days, he reverts to injured reserve for the rest of the season. Crawford suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers. This was the first week he was eligible to return. Questionable for Arizona is all of Budda Baker (groin), Zaven Collins (hip), Kitan Crawford (ankle) and Blake Gillikin (back). Neither Baker or Collins practiced on Friday while Crawford and Gillikin did in limited fashion. For the Rams, both Kam Curl (ankle) and Trent McDuffie (groin) are questionable entering the weekend. Neither practiced on Friday for Los Angeles. "You got Jimmy Lake as kind of his right hand man in the defensive backfield, so there's definitely technique changes and different coverages and tools that they're using. And then I think just probably building it when when they had Myles [Garrett] too in terms of some of the stuff they were doing. So they throw a lot out at you. I asked him the other day. I said, 'So which one are you going to go with? You go with this, or you going to go with that?' And I just got a little chuckle. So, we'll see, and we'll be ready for it all." ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a lengthy injury report entering this weekend's clash with the Los Angeles Rams. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur dove deeper into Love's absence, which you can read about here . Off the Cardinals' injury report is all of Carson Beck (back), Devin Duvernay (ribs), Isaac Seumalo (rest) and Josh Sweat (rest). The likes of Davis Allen (foot), Alex Bachman (wrist), Tyler Higbee (rest), Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), Colby Parkinson (shoulder), Omar Speights (knee), Kegan Trost (hamstring), Josh Wallace (shoulder) and Byron Young (rest) were fully removed from Los Angeles' injury report and are good to go. It's a familiar battle for both sides entering the week, as LaFleur spent the last few seasons under head coach Sean McVay in Los Angeles as the team's offensive coordinator, putting him against Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula. "There's obviously familiarity with just going against him for two of the three years. First year was with Raheem [Morris], but that defense has evolved a lot over the last — since he took over to last year to this year. Obviously, similar foundations and characteristics, but they definitely put their new little twists on it," LaFleur said on facing Shula on Sunday. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." Associated Press Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:59 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love won't play for the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams because of a lingering left ankle injury. "There's no discussion of IR or anything like that," first-year coach Mike LaFleur said. "We've got to re-evaluate, really every single day. Not good enough obviously right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him." Love has been a big part of the Cardinals' offense through the first five weeks with a team-high 245 yards rushing and a touchdown. He's also caught 11 passes for 36 yards and a TD. "He's doing good, but you guys see the way he cuts, just being candid, he cuts hard, that's a superpower of his," LaFleur said. "And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right right now." The Cardinals (1-4) enter Sunday's game against the Rams (2-3) on a four-game losing streak and have lost eight straight games against NFC West opponents. See AP's full NFL coverage here

picks.headline: Chargers vs. Chiefs Score Prediction for NFL Week 6 (Can Kansas City Rout an AFC West Foe?)
picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Chiefs Score Prediction for NFL Week 6 (Can Kansas City Rout an AFC West Foe?) Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Fresh off of a bye week, Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs host the most disappointing team in the NFL in Week 6 – the Los Angeles Chargers. Justin Herbert and the Chargers have yet to win a game this season, going from a preseason darling to one of the worst teams in the NFL. Not only are the Chargers winless, but they have yet to cover the spread and rank in the bottom half of the league in almost every key metric. So, this isn’t a case of a tough schedule messing up L.A.’s playoff chances. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are undefeated and appear to be back in the mix for the No. 1 seed in the AFC after a six-win 2025 campaign. Kenneth Walker III has totally transformed a Kansas City offense that ranks in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play, yards per play and success rate in 2026. Oddsmakers have set Mahomes and Co. as massive favorites at home in this AFC West clash, but can they cover? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game – a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! This AFC West matchup has major implications for the Chiefs as they eye the No. 1 seed in the conference, especially since they already had their bye. Let’s dive right into the odds and my score prediction for Sunday’s game. Chargers vs. Chiefs Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chargers +8.5 (-115) Chiefs -8.5 (-105) Chargers: +380 42.5 (Over -108/Under -112) The total in this matchup has dropped a point since open , but the Chiefs remain 8.5-point favorites at home against a Chargers team that has yet to get a win in 2026. Los Angeles is 0-4-1 against the spread after failing to cover against Denver in Week 5. Chargers vs. Chiefs Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s taking the OVER in this matchup: Don't look now, but the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs once again have one of the best offenses in football. They lead the league in yards per play, averaging 6.5 yards per snap, and they also rank fourth in EPA per play and fifth in offensive success rate. Led by Offensive Player of the Year favorite Kenneth Walker, they're a dangerous offense to face, and any game they're involved in shouldn't have a total in the low 40s. Unfortunately, the Chargers' offense is bad, but I continue to believe that Mike McDaniel's system is going to eventually click, and they're going to have some strong offensive outputs sooner rather than later. Now that they face an average Chiefs defense facing an 0-6 record to start the season, now could be the time that their offense comes out firing. While I don’t mind the OVER play, I think this is going to be a lopsided game, especially since Los Angeles is banged up across the board on offense. Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris have all been hurt in 2026, and the Chargers have tackle Rashawn Slater on injured reserve. That’s led to a terrible offense, as L.A. ranks 32nd in the NFL in EPA/Play and 28th in success rate through five weeks. As MacMillan mentioned, this Chiefs offense has been one of the best in the league, and I expect Patrick Mahomes and Co. to take care of business out of a bye week against a Chargers team that has a very slim chance of turning this season around. L.A. has yet to cover the spread in a game this season, and bettors should expect that to change on Sunday. The Chiefs had a bye in Week 5, but Rice won't be able to recover in time to face the Los Angeles Chargers Sunday. Rice was ruled out for Week 6, but coach Andy Reid said Rice could be back for Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs have just four healthy receivers after Tyquan Thornton went on Injured Reserve. They could activate newly acquired Justin Watson, who signed to the practice squad this week. There's still a large void at the position after quarterback Patrick Mahomes lost two of his top-three receivers. Bold Prediction No. 1: Running Back Emmett Johnson Sees Largest Workload The Chiefs have been singing the fifth-round pick's praise since training camp. He has done everything the team has asked and done it well. However, with running back Kenneth Walker III running all over opposing defenses, Johnson has just 16 rushes for 56 yards and five receptions for 74 yards. The Chiefs have hinted that a larger role was coming for the rookie, but it hasn't happened yet. The Chargers have been a midrange team in defending the running back position. Look for Johnson to be more of a target on checkdown and underneath routes. He'll receive seven to 10 carries and five-plus targets as a receiver. Bold Prediction No. 2: Travis Kelce Goes Over 100 Yards Kelce has 16 catches for 246 yards and two touchdowns on the season. His 15.4 yards per catch would easily be a career high. He looks to be in better shape this season and has broken multiple big gains. Mahomes will look to him as his top option with Rice out as wide receiver Xavier Worthy has yet to show his big-play ability this season. Kelce generally plays well against the Chargers. He caught nine balls for 117 yards and a touchdown in two games against them last season. In 2024, he caught 12 receptions for 134 yards against them. Look for Kelce to snag six to eight receptions for over 100 yards.

Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Chargers vs. Chiefs bold predictions for AFC West clash in Week 6 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers visit the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday with their seasons moving in opposite directions. Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. Speaking to the media on Friday afternoon, Chiefs HC Andy Reid ruled out WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) and LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 6. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

away.blurb: Josh Jacobos could return soon with the Green Bay Packers. The Green Bay Packers have received a major update regarding Josh Jacobs as the star running back moves closer to a potential return. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Jacobs is set to be removed from the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt List on Monday, opening the door for him to rejoin the team as Green Bay prepares for the next stage of the 2026 NFL season. According to Schefter’s report, Josh Jacobs is expected to be eligible to return in Week 7, when the Packers are scheduled to face the Detroit Lions on October 25. However, his removal from the exempt list does not necessarily guarantee that he will play, as any additional disciplinary action from the NFL could affect his availability. Jacobs’ potential return would provide a significant boost to Green Bay’s offense. The running back has been a central part of the team’s attack, and his absence has forced the Packers to rely on other options in the backfield. Having him available again could give quarterback Jordan Love another dependable weapon as the team enters a demanding stretch of its schedule. For now, the Packers must focus on their Week 6 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys while awaiting Jacobs’ expected return. The NFL’s investigation remains open, and the possibility of further discipline means some uncertainty will continue even after Monday’s anticipated roster development. If Jacobs is cleared to play in Week 7, his return against Detroit could be an important moment for Green Bay’s season. He is expected to be eligible to return in Week 7 against the Lions. home.headline: Packers’ Latest Bombshell Micah Parsons Report Is Bad News
home.blurb: NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that the earliest realistic return date for Parsons is Nov. 8 against the New England Patriots. That timeline would keep the All-Pro off the field for the first eight games of the 17-game regular season. A Nov. 8 debut would put Parsons right around the halfway point of the schedule. Missing the Patriots game as well would push his absence past half the season, matching earlier projections from June that he could sit out upwards of half the year following ACL surgery. Running back Josh Jacobs, who had also been unavailable, received positive news Friday when the NFL removed him from the commissioner’s exempt list. He is cleared to return to practice and can play when the Packers visit the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25. If Parsons returns for the Patriots, he would be available for later matchups against the Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Chicago Bears and Houston Texans. Packers' Latest Bombshell Micah Parsons Report Is Bad News NFL AFC North Notre Dame Women's Basketball San Francisco Giants Trade Rumors South Carolina Women's Basketball St. Louis Cardinals Trade Rumors The Green Bay Packers appear increasingly likely to go without star edge rusher Micah Parsons until at least mid-November as he continues recovering from a serious knee injury. “The soonest Parsons appears to have a realistic chance of returning is November 8 against the Patriots,” Pelissero wrote . The Packers have compiled a 3-2 record through five games without Parsons. They sit second in the NFC North behind the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Green Bay’s defense has recorded 14 sacks in those five contests. Lukas Van Ness leads the team with 2.5 sacks while the unit adjusts to life without its top pass rusher. Parsons tore his ACL and suffered meniscus damage on Dec. 14, 2025, in a loss to the Denver Broncos. He underwent surgery on Dec. 29 and remains on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He is now roughly 9½ months removed from the procedure. In 14 games last season after arriving via trade, Parsons posted 12.5 sacks, 41 tackles, 27 quarterback hits and two forced fumbles. He earned first-team All-Pro honors and a Pro Bowl selection for the fifth time. The Packers acquired him from the Dallas Cowboys in August 2025, sending defensive tackle Kenny Clark plus first-round picks in 2026 and 2027 in exchange. Green Bay then signed him to a four-year extension worth approximately $188 million. Green Bay faces a challenging stretch before the Nov. 8 window, starting with a Sunday night matchup against the Cowboys. The schedule also includes a trip to Detroit and a Thursday night home game against the Carolina Panthers. His presence has been viewed as a potential difference-maker for a Packers team looking to contend in the second half of the season after a solid start without him. home.headline: Packers roster moves: WR Savion Williams activated, 3 players go to IR
home.blurb: The most positive news was that wide receiver Savion Williams has been activated from injured reserve, putting him back on the 53-man roster and potentially in the mix to play a role against Dallas. Williams has been limited in practice all week as he ramps up his return from an ankle injury which landed him on IR to start the season. He is questionable for Sunday’s game. After a fairly anonymous rookie year, Williams impressed at training camp with some splash plays and there was plenty of optimism he could have an increased role in Year 2. The injury set him back, but with Jayden Reed out for the year and Skyy Moore also hurt (more on him in a moment), the opportunity is certainly there. The latter two players are unproven, with only 154 defensive snaps in the NFL between them. Help could be on the way though, as Jordon Riley is back at practice after his own Achilles tendon tear. He is doubtful to play on Sunday but could be back on the field in the coming weeks. There was one notable transaction which did not take place, and that was the elevation of a cornerback to the active roster. Brandon Cisse was added to the injury report on Friday with a hip issue, while Benjamin St-Juste has already been ruled out with a hamstring. The fact there was no elevation at corner likely means Cisse’s injury will not keep him out of the game against Dallas. Saturday was a busy day at 1265 Lombardi Avenue, as the Green Bay Packers made six roster moves ahead of Sunday night’s contest with the Dallas Cowboys. On the negative side of the ledger, Green Bay placed three players on injured reserve, including Moore with what is reportedly a high-ankle sprain. The other players were Javon Hargrave, who will miss the rest of the year after tearing his Achilles tendon, and Jonathan Ford due to a calf injury. Injuries at defensive tackle have left the Packers fairly thin at the position. No defensive tackles were elevated for Sunday’s game, meaning they will roll with only four players: Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Chris McClellan and Anthony Campbell. The final two transactions from Saturday were practice squad elevations for the Cowboys game, as edge rusher Arron Mosby and wide receiver Coleman Owen were both brought up to the active roster for "Sunday Night Football." If Williams is not able to play, the Packers would only have had four healthy wide receivers on the active roster in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant. Whether the elevation of Coleman is bad news for Williams’ availability remains to be seen. If Cisse could not go, the Packers would essentially have to elevate someone, as otherwise they would enter the game with only Keisean Nixon, Carrington Valentine and Kamal Hadden as boundary corner options. While he will not play in that many games in 2026, Green Bay is hopeful that his return will take their already impressive defense under Jonathan Gannon to an even higher level. These include defensive stars Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave as well as offensive stars Zach Tom and Jayden Reed. Despite these losses, and terrible play from their offensive line early in year, Green Bay has gone 3-2 in their first five games. The problem is, Amos hasn't been available for quite some time. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants , in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal. "SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!" DC News Now's Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. " Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that's taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated. "Quinn said he'll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return." Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he'll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it's been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil . Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field. "My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it's nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik's been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside," The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account. Amos started training camp on the PUP list but returned to practice a few weeks later … and automatically got hurt again. home.headline: 49ers Owner On Verge of Returning From Lengthy NFL Suspension
home.blurb: The NFL came down hard on York on October 2, handing out a punishment following his arrest for soliciting a prostitute in Ohio that left a lasting stain on his legacy and his family’s legacy as owners of 1 of the NFL’s premier franchises. “49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL’s Personal Conduct Policy, the NFL announced today,” The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero wrote. “During the time the league’s investigation has been proceeding, York has stayed away from the 49ers first three regular-season games, as well as from NFL league meetings. Those three missed games are counted toward his suspension, and he may return on Tuesday, Oct. 20.” 49ers Owner On Verge of Returning From Lengthy NFL Suspension Unlock the latest Heavy on 49ers news — direct to your inbox. San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York knew enough about how the NFL works to stay away from his team for the first 3 weeks of the season. Those weeks would eventually count toward a 6-game suspension that ends after his unbeaten team faces the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 6. How York is received when he returns — if he begins to come around the team again — is another issue entirely after his arrest for soliciting prostitution in Ohio this summer. NFL Came Down Hard on 49ers Owner Jed York “Just in: San Francisco 49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL’s Personal Conduct Policy,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account following the suspension. York was arrested on August 23 at the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in East Palestine, Ohio, as part of an online prostitution sting conducted by local authorities. “Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full,” York said in a prepared statement . “To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one’s failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don’t take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead.” Jed York Stayed Away From 49ers After Arrest York stayed away from the 49ers since his arrest and while the NFL conducted its investigation — the 49ers are now 5-0 and one of just three remaining unbeaten teams.
